title: Java Class Attributes
learningObjectives: Declare instance fields inside a Java class.
Initialize fields at declaration or through a constructor.
Distinguish instance fields from static class fields.
Explain default values for fields that are not explicitly initialized.
Read and update accessible fields through an object reference.

understand.concept: Class attributes, commonly called fields, store data associated with a class or its objects. Instance fields belong to each object separately. Static fields belong to the class and are shared by its instances. Fields receive default values if no explicit initialization is provided.
understand.whyItMatters: Fields hold the information an object needs to perform its responsibilities. Choosing instance or static storage correctly prevents accidental sharing or duplication of state.
understand.analogy: Think of a well-designed object as a small service with a clear responsibility: it keeps the information it owns and exposes only the operations other code needs.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy is only a design aid; Java access, inheritance and dispatch follow the language's exact rules.

explain.narrative:
## Instance fields

Declare fields inside a class but outside its methods. Every object receives its own instance field values. Initialize them directly or assign them in a constructor.

## Static fields

A field declared with `static` belongs to the class rather than one instance. Access it using the class name when possible, such as `Settings.limit`.

## Default values

Fields receive defaults such as `0` for int, `false` for boolean and `null` for reference types. Local variables do not receive these defaults and must be assigned before use.

## Common mistakes

- Making a field static when each object needs its own value.
- Expecting a local variable to have a default value.
- Accessing a private field directly from another class.

examples.title: Instance field values
examples.code:
class Student { String name; }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Student s = new Student(); s.name = "Mina"; System.out.println(s.name); } }
examples.explanation: The name field stores data on the Student instance.

examples.title: Separate instance attributes
examples.code:
class Meter { int reading; }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Meter a = new Meter(); Meter b = new Meter(); a.reading = 12; b.reading = 30; System.out.println(a.reading + b.reading); } }
examples.explanation: Each Meter object has a distinct reading field.

examples.title: A static field is shared
examples.code:
class Visit { static int count = 0; Visit() { count++; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { new Visit(); new Visit(); System.out.println(Visit.count); } }
examples.explanation: The static count field is shared and updated by each constructor call.

examples.title: Field default values
examples.code:
class Defaults { int number; boolean active; String name; }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Defaults d = new Defaults(); System.out.println(d.number + ":" + d.active + ":" + d.name); } }
examples.explanation: Fields receive default values when not explicitly initialized.

examples.title: Initialize a field at declaration
examples.code:
class Plan { int days = 7; }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(new Plan().days); } }
examples.explanation: The field initializer runs when the object is created.

questions.prompt: Where is an instance field declared?
questions.answer: Inside a class and outside its methods
options: Inside a class and outside its methods
questions.explanation: Fields are class members declared outside methods and constructors.

questions.prompt: What does static mean for a field?
questions.answer: It belongs to the class and is shared
options: It belongs to the class and is shared
Each object gets a separate copy
questions.explanation: A static field is associated with the class itself.

questions.prompt: What is the default value of an int field?
questions.explanation: Numeric integer fields default to zero.

questions.prompt: Which value does an uninitialized reference field receive by default?
Which statement about local variables is correct?
questions.answer: They must be assigned before they are read
options: They must be assigned before they are read
questions.explanation: Java's definite-assignment rules require local variables to be initialized before use.
